review.status: No concrete blocker found in the final merge-and-write delta. This is a narrow source review; final GPU tests and performance remain root-owned.
review.scope: iteration1/collectives.cu to current collectives.cu only, with unchanged Layout/ArgBest and provider output/workspace/error contracts checked at their direct anchors.

checks.subject: K1 output order and byte strides
checks.finding: For output logical index l and inner stride-domain size i, ordered_output(l,1)=((floor(l/i))*i+(l mod i))*width=l*width. The old transforms therefore read selected[l]. The new CTA row=l writes values[l]/indices[l], with the identical Layout.read<T>(input,l*width+selected.index). Non-last axes, padded/unaligned/zero-stride input views retain the original address mapping; no dense trailing-axis assumption is added.

checks.subject: NaNs, ties, I32 and original result bits
checks.finding: The unchanged ArgBest comparator reduces the same partial pairs with the same largest flag. Numeric-vs-NaN policy, original lowest-axis-index ties, signed-zero/all-NaN selection and INT32_MAX sentinel remain unchanged. Accumulation<int32_t> remains int64_t; no I32-to-F32 conversion appears. Only the source T is reread and stored, rather than narrowing the comparison score to T. This source property does not replace the focused bitwise GPU test.

checks.subject: BlockReduce participation and stream visibility
checks.finding: All 256 threads reach BlockReduce exactly once, including threads with no partial to load. A single CTA owns each output row; only thread0 reads the selected source value and writes each dense output pair. There is no shared-storage reuse or divergent early return. Stage1 then stage2 launch on the same original stream; stage2 observes every partial. The cold attribute query now names arg_finish_kernel<T> for each actual input type.

checks.subject: Workspace removal
checks.finding: The tiled configure branch now returns after reserving the checked, 256-aligned rows*tiles*sizeof(ArgPair<Acc>) partial array. Stage2 writes public outputs directly, so the old selected array and CUB transform scratch are unnecessary. The selected/temporary pointer locals still computed in submit are never dereferenced by the tiled branch, which returns before both DeviceTransform calls. They do not require separate backing. The original workspace extent/alignment validation remains. Tile-count multiplication and round-up overflow checks are unchanged.

checks.subject: Independent outputs and accepted-prefix failures
checks.finding: The provider still requires the exact dense inferred outputs, aligned T/I32 destinations, and grants no alias support. Direct writes cannot overwrite permitted source/workspace aliases. Stage1 failure returns its launch error; stage2 failure returns its launch error after the accepted stage1 prefix. The unchanged provider synchronizes its accepted managed error path and returns accepted_command(status), so retirement semantics are retained. No hot allocation, synchronization or host payload read is added by this delta.

checks.subject: Private ABI and neighboring domains
checks.finding: Header and provider hashes are unchanged from iteration1. The private Program layout was already refreshed with the iteration1 provider object; this CU-only change needs no additional provider recompilation for layout reasons. TopK0/count0, R1, width<=2048 multirow, K>1, Scan and Gather remain on their existing branches. Public API/ID/capture capability is unchanged.

ready_baseline.definition: Last process-running sample between received ready and earliest actual prefill-begin; null when none exists.

limits: All boundaries are parent receipt times from live stderr, not exact device/allocator times. Phase names are discovered from actual markers, including session prefixes.

PSAPI/PDH sampled maxima are lower bounds, not physical allocation totals. Dedicated/shared separate maxima must not be added; total uses simultaneous available counters.
Neighbor-sample phase deltas include bracket age and may include subsequent work or teardown; they do not attribute allocations or frees.
Old runs whose observer dropped session-prefixed markers cannot have timestamped phase samples reconstructed from untimestamped stderr. This adapter does not rewrite them.
Memory sampling is independent and never contributes to unmonitored timing denominators.
